answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to optofluidic fluorescence cells. A node proves authenticity by pumping fluorophores through a capillary inlet, sampling luminescence decay excited by a violet laser across an attestation thread. An attacker must operate discrete microfluidic chambers per identity, incurring ongoing chemical and hardware fabrication costs. However, cumulative photobleaching steadily degrades optical fidelity.
